title: All Fields Reference
description: Every field the standard defines, in one file, for building forms, interfaces and tables against. The envelope is reproduced from record.schema.json; each type's payload is in $defs as data_<type>. This is a real schema and validates real records — `data` must match the payload for the declared `type`. Regenerate with build-all-fields.mjs after changing any schema.

$schema.description: Optional self-identification on instance documents, so editors can offer completion.

id.description: Stable internal identity. Never reused, never changes for the life of the record.

uri.description: Dereferenceable identity. Pattern: https://mdm.cameron-dietz.com/id/{type}/{id}. When six apps pass a reference around, a resolvable URI is unambiguous in a way a bare UUID is not.

type.description: Entity type. Drives which type schema applies and how `data` is interpreted. Types with a payload definition in $defs: content_category, document, employment, item, location, organization, person, place.

slug.description: Human-readable handle for URLs and filenames. Unique within a type. Kebab-case ids like 'nims-doctrine-2023' belong here, not in `id`.

label.description: Display name. Present on EVERY record so unified search, pickers and link previews can render any result without knowing its payload shape.

summary.description: One-paragraph plain-language description, for search snippets and hover cards.

aliases.description: Alternate names, abbreviations, former names, common misspellings. Feed into the search index; also the cheapest deduplication signal when merging sources.

category.description: Faceted classification: dimension -> value(s). Dimensions are independent axes that do not collide with each other. Depth WITHIN a dimension uses dots, so hierarchy is a prefix match rather than a closure table. Open map: new dimensions need no schema change.

tags.description: Uncontrolled freeform keywords for full-text search. Anything you intend to facet, filter or report on belongs in `category` instead.

status.description: Record lifecycle: is this entry current and usable? Orthogonal to `state`.

state.description: Domain condition, orthogonal to `status`. An item can be status=active and state=out_of_service at the same time.

version.description: Human revision label of this record as a whole.

data_schema.description: Optional URI of the schema `data` conforms to. Payload versioning lives here: bump the URI on a breaking payload change and old records keep pointing at the old schema.

superseded_by.description: id of the record replacing this one. Expected whenever status is 'superseded'.

valid_from.description: When the fact became true in the world. Distinct from created_at, which is when the system learned it. Keeping these separate is what lets you ask what was in force on a given date.

valid_to.description: When the fact stopped being true. Null means still in force.

last_verified.description: Last date this record was reconfirmed against its source.

review_due.description: Next scheduled review. One query then finds everything stale across every type at once.

visibility.description: Coarse access tier. This is a LABEL - the serving layer must actually enforce it. Per-group ACLs belong in a separate grants table keyed by record id, not here.

pii.description: Contains personal information. Explicit flag so retention and subject-access sweeps need not parse payloads.

owner.description: Who is accountable for keeping this record correct.

parent_id.description: Canonical containment parent, for hierarchies and ownership. Additional parents go in `relations`; a single containment tree is worth far more than multi-parent flexibility costs.

relations.description: Typed edges to other records. Keeps foreign keys out of `data` so generic tooling can walk the graph without knowing the domain.

identifiers.description: Cross-walk of external identifiers keyed by issuing scheme. How the same real-world entity arriving from three different APIs resolves to one record. Arrays because an entity can hold several ids in one scheme. Index as (scheme, value) -> id.

url.description: Canonical web location of the thing ITSELF - a document's file, an organization's website, a tool's homepage. Not provenance; see source_url.

links.description: Additional named URLs beyond the canonical one.

attachments.description: Files belonging to this record: the PDF, the photo, the featured image, the manual.

source_system.description: Originating system, when this record was imported or synced rather than created here.

source_record_id.description: The record's id in the source system. Paired with source_system this is a natural key that makes re-imports idempotent.

source_url.description: Where this record was obtained. Provenance, not the thing's own address.

checksum_sha256.description: Hash of the record's canonical content. Deduplicates re-imports and detects drift. Exclude volatile fields (updated_at, geo.place_closure, checksum_sha256 itself) before hashing or values will never match across systems.

apps.description: Ids of consuming apps that should treat this record as relevant. Empty array means none yet.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete. Null or absent means live; a timestamp means logically deleted - filter from normal reads without losing history.

metadata.description: Open escape hatch. Because the envelope is strict, new or experimental fields go here instead of at the top level, then get promoted into real fields once they prove out.

data.description: Type-specific payload. The allOf below selects the matching data_<type> definition.

taxon_value.title: Taxonomy Value
taxon_value.description: One or many values on a classification dimension. Dots denote layers within the dimension, so 'emergency_management.hazmat' is matched by a prefix query for 'emergency_management'. Readers normalize with: v == null ? [] : Array.isArray(v) ? v : [v].

actor_ref.title: Actor Reference
actor_ref.description: A person, service, automation or the system itself.

label.description: Display snapshot so a UI needs no second lookup. Not the source of truth.

relation.title: Relation
relation.description: A plain edge. Relationships carrying their own attributes or dates - employment, licensing, approval - get their own record type instead.

rel.description: Role the target plays relative to this record.

label.description: Display snapshot so a UI can render the link without a join.

primary.description: Marks the principal edge when several share the same rel.

attachment.title: Attachment
attachment.description: One file. Use `path` for something stored in your own repo or bucket, `href` for something remote.

position.title: Position
position.description: [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation_m]. WGS84 / EPSG:4326 only. LONGITUDE COMES FIRST - GeoJSON order, the reverse of how humans, CAP alerts and most spreadsheets write coordinates, and the single most common bug in geospatial integrations. The per-slot bounds here catch a flip at validation time: [30.2672, -97.7431] fails because -97.74 is not a valid latitude.

linear_ring.description: Closed ring: first and last positions identical, exterior rings counterclockwise, holes clockwise. JSON Schema cannot express 'first element equals last', so only the 4-position minimum is enforced here - assert closure and winding in ingest code. CAP/IPAWS polygons in particular arrive as lat,lon pairs and frequently need both a flip and an explicit close.

geometry.title: GeoJSON Geometry
geometry.description: RFC 7946 geometry object. Store WGS84 and project at display time.

bbox.title: Bounding Box
bbox.description: [west, south, east, north]. Cheap pre-filter before real geometry math, and enough to fit a map viewport.

address.title: Postal Address
address.description: schema.org PostalAddress field names, snake-cased. Uses address_region rather than 'state' so non-US data needs no parallel shape.

formatted.description: Single-string rendering for display, and for matching sources that only give you one blob.

shape.title: Shape
shape.description: One geometry plus what it MEANS. A record can carry several: a repeater has a site point and a coverage polygon; an agency has a headquarters and a jurisdiction. Role is what lets one query ask the right question of every type.

circle.description: CAP/IPAWS-style circle. GeoJSON has no circle primitive, so keep the authoritative parameters here AND write a derived polygon into `geometry` for anything doing spatial math.

precision_m.description: Approximate positional uncertainty in meters. A rooftop geocode and a ZIP centroid are not the same fact.

simplified.description: Display-resolution copy. Never run analysis against it.

geo.title: Geography
geo.description: All location information, on the envelope rather than inside `data`, so 'what is near here' and 'what is in this county' work identically across every type in the catalog.

point.description: Single canonical point for mapping, sorting and distance. For an area, use a point guaranteed to fall INSIDE it (point-on-surface), not the centroid - the centroid of a crescent-shaped county is outside the county.

precision.description: How precisely `point` was determined. Drives whether you may render it as a pin, a circle, or a shaded area. Never show a ZIP-centroid point as a rooftop pin.

place_closure.description: DERIVED AT WRITE TIME: every place in `places`, plus all ancestors, plus every place containing `point` or intersecting `shapes`. Turns 'everything in Travis County' into one array-contains lookup with no geometry engine involved. Never edit by hand.

timezone.description: IANA zone, derived from location. Stored so downstream apps render local times without a lookup service.

data_content_category.title: content_category payload
data_content_category.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "content_category".

seo.description: Search-engine metadata. Kept in the payload because it is a presentation concern of one website, not a fact about the entity.

title.description: Overrides `label` in the page title tag when set.

keywords.description: Distinct from envelope `tags`: these are phrases aimed at search engines, tags are for your own retrieval. They will often differ in casing and wording.

display.description: Presentation controls for the category page.

sort_order.description: Manual ordering among siblings; lower sorts first.

data_document.title: document payload
data_document.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "document".

publisher.description: Issuing body as plain text. When the publisher exists as an organization record, add a relations entry with rel='publisher' as well - the string stays for display and for sources you never model.

publication_date.description: Publisher's original publication date. YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM / YYYY when that is all that is known - which is why this is not format: date.

abstract.description: Longer than `summary`, which stays short enough for search snippets.

citation.description: Formatted citation string for reuse in other documents.

data_employment.title: employment payload
data_employment.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "employment".

employment_type.description: Null when the source system did not say.

work_email.description: Work contact lives here, not on the person, because it changes when the job does.

office.description: Free-text office name. The office as a real site goes in relations as rel='office_location'.

compensation.description: Almost always warrants visibility=confidential on the whole record.

data_item.title: item payload
data_item.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "item".

features.description: Specifications as key/value pairs. Open because every product family has different ones; when a family stabilizes, give it its own data_schema rather than guessing a universal spec model.

list_minor.description: List price in MINOR units - cents, not dollars. Integers only; never store money as a float.

serial_number.description: Only for a record tracking ONE physical unit. A product-model record has no serial; put it in identifiers.serial if you track units as separate records.

lifecycle.description: Dates about the physical unit, distinct from the record's own valid_from/valid_to.

data_location.title: location payload
data_location.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "location".

hours.description: OSM opening_hours syntax if you want it machine-readable, free text otherwise.

access_notes.description: Gate codes, dock instructions, badge requirements. Often warrants visibility=restricted on the whole record.

data_organization.title: organization payload
data_organization.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "organization".

legal_name.description: Registered legal name when it differs from the common name in `label`, e.g. 'Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc.'

ownership.description: Ownership and corporate-structure facts that are not themselves records. A parent company that exists in the system belongs in parent_id or relations instead.

contact.description: Main switchboard contact, not a person's contact.

naics.description: NAICS industry codes. Kept here rather than in identifiers because these classify the org, they do not identify it.

data_person.title: person payload
data_person.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "person".

full_name.description: Complete name as normally written. Keep it even when derivable from the parts - name order is not universal, and the envelope `label` may be styled differently (e.g. 'Dietz, Cameron').

birth_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Sensitive: consider visibility=restricted, or omit entirely for records that feed public directories.

roles.description: Functional roles independent of any employer, e.g. 'incident commander', 'notary'. Job titles belong on the employment record.

skills.description: Capabilities and qualifications. Certifications with expiry dates deserve their own record type rather than a bare string here.

contact.description: Personal contact methods. Work contact belongs on the employment record, because it changes when the job does.

data_place.title: place payload
data_place.description: Everything `data` may hold when type is "place".

adm_level.description: Depth in the administrative hierarchy: 0 country, 1 state/region, 2 county, 3 locality. Lets you query a whole tier without enumerating kinds.

boundary_source.description: Which authoritative dataset the boundary geometry came from, and its vintage.
